lead.headline: INDIA EDGE PAKISTAN IN LAST-BALL U-19 ASIA CUP FINAL THRILLER
lead.deck: Mohit Ulva’s boundary off the final delivery completed a one-wicket chase of 338 in Oman and gave India a record ninth title.
paragraphs: India beat Pakistan by one wicket in a dramatic Under-19 Asia Cup final at Al Amerat, chasing down 338 on the last ball.
Pakistan had set the imposing target after posting 337 for nine. India’s chase faltered late, but Mohit Ulva and Manal Chauhan kept the side in contention with a decisive ninth-wicket stand.
Ulva struck the winning boundary from the final delivery, sealing India’s ninth title in the competition.

sidebarStory.headline: PINK LINE STRETCH OPENS AS BENGALURU METRO NETWORK CROSSES 100 KM
sidebarStory.subhead: The 7.5-km elevated section from Kalena Agrahara to Tavarekere began commercial service on Saturday, adding a key south Bengaluru connection.
paragraphs: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the elevated stretch of the Pink Line on November 14, and passenger services began the same day.
The new section extends the city’s metro network beyond 100 km. The remaining underground stretch is expected to open later, completing the line towards Nagawara.

groups.ariaLabel: Bengaluru and Karnataka city, public safety and governance news

stories.headline: HIGH COURT SEEKS DIGITAL TREE RECORD TO PREVENT CITY HAZARDS
paragraphs: Karnataka High Court pressed for a digital system to monitor Bengaluru’s trees and reduce risks from hazardous or falling trees.
The proposal would help authorities track trees and respond to safety concerns across the city.

stories.headline: ED ATTACHES ₹1.22 CRORE ASSETS IN KPSC RECRUITMENT SCAM
paragraphs: The Enforcement Directorate attached assets worth ₹1.22 crore in its investigation into alleged irregularities in Karnataka Public Service Commission recruitment.
The action adds a financial investigation to a case drawing scrutiny over the integrity of public-service hiring.

stories.headline: CHILDREN USE INSECT COSTUMES TO PROTEST PROPOSED HEBBAL LAKE TUNNEL
paragraphs: Children dressed as butterflies, ants and other insects gathered at Hebbal Lake to oppose the proposed short tunnel project and raise concerns about green-space loss.
The young protesters used placards and costumes to draw attention to the lake’s ecology and the impact of construction on the area.

groups.ariaLabel: India air quality, weather and national security news

stories.headline: CENTRE ORDERS 191 POLLUTING UNITS SEALED, FIXES OFFICIALS’ ACCOUNTABILITY
paragraphs: With Delhi’s air nearing the severe category, the Centre ordered 191 non-compliant polluting industries in the National Capital Region sealed.
States were asked to nominate senior officials to oversee implementation of pollution-control measures across the region.

stories.headline: LOW-PRESSURE SYSTEM MAY STRENGTHEN INTO CYCLONE BY NOVEMBER 16
paragraphs: A well-marked low-pressure area over the southeast Bay of Bengal is forecast to intensify and move northwest.
The IMD said a cyclonic storm may form over the central south and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal around the evening of November 16.

stories.headline: COURT DENIES BAIL TO TWO MEN IN 2023 PARLIAMENT SECURITY BREACH CASE
paragraphs: A Delhi court rejected bail pleas by two accused in the Parliament security breach case.
The case concerns the 2023 incident in which intruders entered the Lok Sabha chamber and released coloured smoke.

groups.ariaLabel: India education, economy and sport news

stories.headline: NTA SETS UP PERMANENT OBSERVER POOL AFTER NEET-UG PAPER LEAK
paragraphs: The National Testing Agency is building a permanent pool of independent observers as part of changes following the NEET-UG paper leak earlier this year.
The proposed pool includes retired armed-forces and government personnel who would monitor examinations separately from local centre officials.

stories.headline: FIR REGISTERED OVER KANGANA RANAUT’S SOCIAL MEDIA POST
paragraphs: Himachal Pradesh Police registered an FIR over a November 10 post on BJP MP Kangana Ranaut’s X account.
Police said the post contained alleged remarks about members of the Gandhi family, including former prime ministers Indira Gandhi and Rajiv Gandhi.

stories.headline: CBI SEARCHES 33 LOCATIONS ACROSS SIX STATES IN MAHADEV APP CASE
paragraphs: The CBI searched 33 locations across six states in its investigation into the Mahadev online betting app case.
Investigators recovered phones, digital devices and documents that officials said point to alleged mule bank accounts and hawala channels.

stories.headline: INDIA FINISH THIRD WITH 13 MEDALS AT WORLD CHAMPIONSHIPS
paragraphs: India closed the Doha World Shooting Championships with 13 medals—two gold, seven silver and four bronze—to finish third in the standings.
China topped the table and Italy placed second as the two-week rifle, pistol and shotgun competition concluded.

listing: Performances continue at Alliance Française de Bangalore through Sunday evening.
Poetry and conversation with Javed Akhtar and Shabana Azmi runs from 4:30 to 6:30 p.m.

stories.headline: PARTLY CLOUDY TODAY; NO CITY WARNING IN FORCE

paragraphs: The IMD forecast for Bengaluru on Sunday is partly cloudy skies, with a minimum of 17°C and maximum of 29°C. No warning is in force.
